decision: Apply the named Akerøy fort geometry on Festningsholmen and retain the main island Akerøya only as a separate geographic and protection context.
identityFindings: Akerøy fort is situated on Festningsholmen, a small islet beside Akerøya, not at the legacy point on the eastern side of the main island.
OSM way 289950084 and Wikidata Q3078124 identify the fortification itself.
Hvaler municipality uses the name Akerøy fort and presents 1664 as the establishment year.
The main island Akerøya is a separate geographic object with OSM way 296238827, Wikidata Q1770613 and GeoNames 9063813.
chronologyFindings: Hvaler municipality presents the fort as built in 1664.
Store norske leksikon describes an initial fortification around 1660 and later reinforcement in 1675, 1744 and 1788.
Sources vary between 1807 and 1808 for the demolition of the fort.
The state sold the remains in 1850, and organised voluntary restoration began in 1962.
The canonical year 1664 is retained as the municipality's foundation year while the text preserves the multi-phase development.

accessAndProtection.mainIslandContext: Akerøya lies in Ytre Hvaler National Park and parts of the main island have seasonal access restrictions.
accessAndProtection.fortContext: The fort lies on the separate Festningsholmen. Restrictions documented for the main island must not be automatically projected onto the fort islet without checking the current official protection map.
